source_text:
Ἵνα δὲ ἐπιθαρρήσῃς, οὕτω μετανοήσας ἀληθῶς, ὅτι σοὶ μένει σωτηρίας ἐλπὶς ἀξιόχρεως, ἄκουσον μῦθον οὐ μῦθον, ἀλλὰ ὄντα λόγον περὶ Ἰωάννου τοῦ ἀποστόλου παραδεδομένον καὶ μνήμῃ πεφυλαγμένον. ἐπειδὴ γὰρ τοῦ τυράννου τελευτήσαντος ἀπὸ τῆς Πάτμου τῆς νήσου μετῆλθεν ἐπὶ τὴν Ἔφεσον. ἀπῄει παρακαλούμενος καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ πλησιόχωρα τῶν ἐθνῶν, ὅπου μὲν ἐπισκόπους καταστήσων. ὅπου δὲ ὅλας ἐκκλησίας ἁρμόσων, ὅπου δὲ κλῆρον ἕνα γέ τινα κληρώσων τῶν ὑπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος σημαινομένων. ἐλθὼν οὖν καὶ ἐπί τινα τῶν οὐ μακρὰν πόλεων, ἧς καὶ τοὔνομα λέγουσιν ἔνιοι, καὶ τὰ ἄλλα ἀναπαύσας τοὺς ἀδελφούς, ἐπὶ πᾶσι τῷ καθεστῶτι προσβλέψας ἐπισκόπῳ. νεανίσκον ἱκανὸν τῷ σώματι καὶ τὴν ὄψιν ἀστεῖον καὶ θερμὸν τὴν ψυχὴν ἰδών, »τοῦτον« ἔφη »σοὶ παρακατατίθεμαι μετὰ πάσης σπουδῆς ἐπὶ τῆς ἐκκλησίας καὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ μάρτυρος«. τοῦ δὲ δεχομένου καὶ πάνθ᾿ ὑπισχνουμένου καὶ πάλιν τὰ αὐτὰ διετείνατο καὶ διεμαρτύρατο. εἶτα ὃ μὲν ἀπῆρεν ἐπὶ τὴν Ἔφεσον, ὁ δὲ πρεσβύτερος ἀναλαβὼν οἴκαδε τὸν παραδοθέντα νεανίσκον ἔτρεφε, συνεῖχεν. ἔθαλπε, τὸ τελευταῖον ἐφώτισε· καὶ μετὰ τοῦτο ὑφῆκε τῆς πλείονος ἐπιμελείας καὶ παραφυλακῆς, ὡς τὸ τέλειον αὐτῷ φυλακτήριον ἐπιστήσας, τὴν σφραγῖδα τοῦ κυρίου. τῷ δὲ ἀνέσεως πρὸ ὥρας λαβομένῳ προσφθείρονταί τινες ἥλικες ἀργοὶ καὶ ἀπερρωγότες, ἐθάδες κακῶν· καὶ πρῶτον μὲν δι᾿ ἑστιάσεων πολυτελῶν αὐτὸν ὑπάγονται. εἶτά που καὶ νύκτωρ ἐπὶ λωποδυσίαν ἐξιόντες συνεπάγονται, εἶτά τι καὶ μεῖζον συμπράττειν ἠξίουν. ὃ δὲ κατ᾿ ὀλίγον προσειθίζετο καὶ διὰ μέγεθος φύσεως ἐκστὰς ὥσπερ ἄστομος καὶ εὔρωστος ἵππος ὀρθῆς ὁδοῦ καὶ τὸν χαλινὸν ἐνδακὼν μειζόνως κατὰ τῶν βαράθρων ἐφέρετο. ἀπογνοὺς δὲ τελέως τὴν ἐν θεῷ σωτηρίαν οὐδὲν ἔτι μικρὸν διενοεῖτο, ἀλλὰ μέγα τι πράξας, ἐπειδήπερ ἅπαξ ἀπολώλει, ἴσα τοῖς ἄλλοις παθεῖν ἠξίου. αὐτοὺς δὴ τούτους ἀναλαβὼν καὶ λῃστήριον συγκροτήσας, ἕτοιμος λῄσταρχος ἦν, βιαιότατος, μιαιφονώτατος, χαλεπώτατος. χρόνος ἐν μέσῳ, καί τινος ἐπιπεσούσης χρείας ἀνακαλοῦσι τὸν Ἰωάννην. ὃ δέ, ἐπεὶ τὰ ἄλλα ὧν χάριν ἧκεν κατεστήσατο, »ἄγε δή«, ἔφη. »ὦ ἐπίσκοπε, τὴν παραθήκην ἀπόδος ἡμῖν, ἣν ἐγώ τε καὶ ὁ Χριστός σοι παρακατεθέμεθα ἐπὶ τῆς ἐκκλησίας, ἧς προκαθέζῃ. μάρτυρος.« ὃ δὲ τὸ μὲν πρῶτον ἐξεπλάγη, χρήματα οἰόμενος. ἅπερ οὐκ ἔλαβε, συκοφαντεῖσθαι, καὶ οὔτε πιστεύειν εἶχεν ὑπὲρ ὧν οὐκ εἶχεν οὔτε ἀπιστεῖν Ἰωάννῃ· ὡς δὲ »τὸν νεανίσκον« εἶπεν »ἀπαιτῶ καὶ τὴν ψυχὴν τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ«, στενάξας κάτωθεν ὁ πρεσβύτης καί τι καὶ ἐπιδακρύσας, »ἐκεῖνος« ἔφη »τέθνηκε«. »πῶς καὶ τίνα θάνατον;« »θεῷ τέθνηκεν« εἶπεν· »ἀπέβη γὰρ πονηρὸς καὶ ἐξώλης καί, τὸ κεφάλαιον. λῃστής, καὶ νῦν ἀντὶ τῆς ἐκκλησίας τὸ ὄρος κατείληφε μεθ᾿ ὁμοίου στρατιωτικοῦ.« καταρρηξάμενος τὴν ἐσθῆτα ὁ ἀπόστολος καὶ μετὰ μεγάλης οἰμωγῆς πληξάμενος τὴν κεφαλήν. »καλόν γε« ἔφη »φύλακα τῆς τἀδελφοῦ ψυχῆς κατέλιπον· ἀλλ᾿ ἵππος ἤδη μοι παρέστω καὶ ἡγεμὼν γενέσθω μοί τις τῆς ὁδοῦ.« ἤλαυνεν, ὥσπερ εἶχεν, αὐτόθεν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας. ἐλθὼν δὲ εἰς τὸ χωρίον ὑπὸ τῆς προφυλακῆς τῶν λῃστῶν ἁλίσκεται, μήτε φεύγων μήτε παραιτούμενος. ἀλλὰ βοῶν· »ἐπὶ τοῦτ᾿ ἐλήλυθα, ἐπὶ τὸν ἄρχοντα ὑμῶν ἀγάγετέ με.« ὃς τέως, ὥσπερ ὥπλιστο, ἀνέμενεν· ὡς δὲ προσιόντα ἐγνώρισε τὸν Ἰωάννην, εἰς φυγὴν αἰδεσθεὶς ἐτράπετο. ὃ δὲ ἐδίωκεν ἀνὰ κράτος, ἐπιλαθόμενος τῆς ἡλικίας τῆς ἑαυτοῦ, κεκραγώς· »τί με φεύγεις, τέκνον, τὸν σαυτοῦ πατέρα, τὸν γυμνόν, τὸν γέροντα; ἐλέησόν με. τέκνον, μή φοβοῦ· ἔχεις ἔτι ζωῆς ἐλπίδας· ἐγὼ χριστῷ λόγον δώσω ὑπὲρ σοῦ· ἂν δέῃ, τὸν σὸν θάνατον ἑκὼν ὑπομενῶ, ὡς ὁ κύριος τὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν· ὑπὲρ σοῦ τὴν ψυχὴν ἀντιδώσω τὴν ἐμήν. στῆθι, πίστευσον· Χριστός με ἀπέστειλεν.« ὃ δὲ ἀκούσας πρῶτον ἔστη μὲν κάτω βλέπων. εἶτα ἔρριψε τὰ ὅπλα, εἶτα τρέμων ἔκλαιε πικρῶς· προσελθόντα δὲ τὸν γέροντα περιέλαβεν, ἀπολογούμενος ταῖς οἰμωγαῖς ὡς ἐδύνατο καὶ τοῖς δάκρυσι βαπτιζόμενος ἐκ δευτέρου. μόνην ἀποκρύπτων τὴν δεξιάν. ὃ δὲ ἐγγυώμενος, ἐπομνύμενος ὡς ἄφεσιν αὐτῷ παρὰ τοῦ σωτῆρος εὕρηται, δεόμενος, γονυπετῶν, αὐτὴν τὴν δεξιὰν ὡς ὑπὸ τῆς μετανοίας κεκαθαρμένην καταφιλῶν, ἐπὶ τὴν ἐκκλησίαν ἐπανήγαγε, καὶ δαψιλέσι μὲν εὐχαῖς ἐξαιτούμενος, συνεχέσι δὲ νηστείαις συναγωνιζόμενος, ποικίλαις δὲ σειρῆσι λόγων κατεπᾴδων αὐτοῦ τὴν γνώμην, οὐ πρότερον ἀπῆλθεν, ὥς φασι, πρὶν αὐτὸν ἐπιστῆσαι τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ, διδοὺς μέγα παράδειγμα μετανοίας ἀληθινῆς καὶ μέγα γνώρισμα παλιγγενεσίας,τρόπαιον ἀναστάσεως βλεπομένης.
* * * φαιδροῖς γεγηθότες, ὑμνοῦντες, ἀνοιγνύντες τοὺς οὐρανούς. πρὸ δὲ πάντων αὐτὸς ὁ σωτὴρ προαπαντᾷ δεξιούμενος, φῶς ὀρέγων ἄσκιον, ἄπαυστον, ὁδηγῶν εἰς τοὺς κόλπους τοῦ πατρός, εἰς τὴν αἰώνιον ζωήν, εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν. πιστευέτω ταῦτά τις καὶ θεοῦ μαθηταῖς καὶ ἐγγυητῇ θεῷ, προφητείαις, εὐαγγελίοις, λόγοις ἀποστολικοῖς· τούτοις συζῶν καὶ τὰ ὦτα ὑπέχων καὶ τὰ ἔργα ἀσκῶν ἐπ᾿ αὐτῆς τῆς ἐξόδου τὸ τέλος καὶ τὴν ἐπίδειξιν τῶν δογμάτων ὄψεται. ὁ γὰρ ἐνταῦθα τὸν ἄγγελον τῆς μετανοίας προσιέμενος οὐ μετανοήσει τότε, ἡνίκα ἂν καταλίπῃ τὸ σῶμα, οὐδὲ καταισχυνθήσεται, τὸν σωτῆρα προσιόντα μετὰ τῆς αὑτοῦ δόξης καὶ στρατιᾶς ἰδών· οὐ δέδιε τὸ πῦρ· εἰ δέ τις αἱρεῖται μένειν ἐπεξαμαρτάνων ἑκάστοτε ἐπὶ ταῖς ἡδοναῖς καὶ τὴν ἐνταῦθα τρυφὴν τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς προτιμᾷ καὶ διδόντος τοῦ σωτῆρος ἄφεσιν ἀποστρέφεται, μήτε τὸν θεὸν ἔτι μήτε τὸν πλοῦτον μήτε τὸ προπεσεῖν αἰτιάσθω, τὴν δὲ ἑαυτοῦ ψυχὴν ἑκουσίως ἀπολουμένην. τῷ δὲ ἐπιβλέποντι τὴν σωτηρίαν καὶ ποθοῦντι καὶ μετὰ ἀναιδείας καὶ βίας αἰτοῦντι παρέξει τὴν ἀληθινὴν κάθαρσιν καὶ τὴν ἄτρεπτον ζωὴν ὁ πατὴρ ὁ ἀγαθὸς ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς. ᾧ διὰ τοῦ παιδὸς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ κυρίου ζώντων καὶ νεκρῶν, καὶ διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος εἴη δόξα, τιμή, κράτος, αἰώνιος μεγαλειότης καὶ νῦν καὶ εἰς γενεὰς γενεῶν καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. ἀμήν.
thought_title: The story of John and the young robber
orientation: Clement is closing his homily by telling the story of the apostle John and a young man who fell into brigandage, as proof that true repentance restores even the fallen.
pass_a_gloss: So that you may take courage, having repented truly in this way, because a sufficient hope of salvation remains for you, hear a story not a story, but a true account about John the apostle, handed down and kept in memory. For when the tyrant had died, he returned from the island of Patmos to Ephesus. He went out, being invited, also to the neighboring regions of the Gentiles, in some places to appoint bishops, in other places to fit together whole churches, in other places to appoint by lot one cleric of those indicated by the Spirit. Having come then also to one of the cities not far away, whose name some also mention, and having refreshed the brothers in other matters, he looked at the appointed bishop above all. Having seen a young man able in body and pleasing in appearance and warm in soul, he said, 'This one I entrust to you with all diligence before the church and Christ as witness.' When he accepted and promised everything, he again insisted on the same things and testified. Then he departed for Ephesus, and the elder took the young man who had been entrusted to him home, nourished him, kept him close, cherished him, and finally baptized him. And after this he relaxed his greater care and watchfulness, as having set upon him the perfect safeguard, the seal of the Lord. But when he got freedom before the right time, some idle and dissolute age-mates, familiar with evils, corrupt him. And first they lead him astray through lavish feasts. Then going out somewhere at night for robbery they take him along, then they thought it right for him to do something greater too. And he gradually became accustomed, and because of the greatness of his nature, having bolted like a hard-mouthed and strong horse from the straight road and biting the bit, he was carried more violently against the pits. Having despaired completely of salvation in God, he no longer planned anything small, but having done some great thing, since he had once and for all perished, he thought it right to suffer the same as the others. Taking these very ones and forming a robber band, he was a ready robber chief, most violent, most murderous, most harsh. Time passed, and when some need fell upon them, they call John back. And he, when he had set in order the other things for which he had come, said, 'Come now, bishop, give back to us the deposit which I and Christ entrusted to you before the church over which you preside, as witness.' And he at first was astonished, thinking that he was being falsely accused about money which he had not received, and he could neither believe about what he did not have nor disbelieve John. But when he said, 'I demand the young man and the soul of the brother,' the elder groaned from deep within and wept a little, and said, 'That one is dead.' 'How and what death?' 'He is dead to God,' he said, 'for he went away wicked and utterly ruined and, in sum, a robber, and now instead of the church he has seized the mountain with a like band of soldiers.' The apostle tore his garment and struck his head with great lamentation, and said, 'A fine guard of the brother's soul I left behind! But let a horse be ready for me now and let someone be my guide on the road.' He rode, just as he was, from there from the church. Having come to the place, he is seized by the robber's advance guard, neither fleeing nor begging off, but crying out, 'For this I have come; lead me to your leader.' He for a while, just as he was armed, waited. But when he recognized John approaching, he turned to flight in shame. And he pursued at full speed, forgetting his own age, crying out, 'Why do you flee me, child, your own father, the naked one, the old man? Have mercy on me, child, do not fear. You still have hopes of life. I will give an account to Christ for you. If it is necessary, I will willingly endure your death, as the Lord did for us. For you I will give my own soul in exchange. Stand, believe. Christ sent me.' And he, having heard, first stood looking down. Then he threw away his weapons, then trembling he wept bitterly. And he embraced the old man as he approached, defending himself with groans as he could and being baptized a second time with tears, hiding only his right hand. And he, pledging, swearing that forgiveness had been found for him from the Savior, begging, kneeling, kissing the very right hand as having been cleansed by repentance, led him back to the church, and with abundant prayers interceding for him, with constant fastings struggling together with him, with varied cords of words charming his mind, he did not depart, as they say, before he set him before the church, giving a great example of true repentance and a great mark of regeneration, a trophy of a resurrection that is seen. * * * rejoicing with bright ones, hymning, opening the heavens. And before all things the Savior himself comes to meet them, welcoming, offering shadowless light, unceasing, leading into the bosom of the father, into eternal life, into the kingdom of heaven. Let someone believe these things, both the disciples of God and God as guarantor, the prophecies, the gospels, the apostolic words. Living with these and lending his ears and practicing the deeds, at the very departure he will see the end and the demonstration of the teachings. For the one who here receives the angel of repentance will not repent then, when he leaves the body, nor will he be put to shame, seeing the Savior coming with his own glory and army. He does not fear the fire. But if someone chooses to remain sinning continually in pleasures and prefers the luxury here to eternal life and turns away from the Savior giving forgiveness, let him blame neither God nor wealth nor his fall, but his own soul perishing willingly. But to the one who looks to salvation and longs for it and asks with shamelessness and force, the good Father in the heavens will provide the true cleansing and the unchanging life. To whom through the child Jesus Christ, the Lord of the living and the dead, and through the Holy Spirit be glory, honor, might, eternal majesty, both now and unto generations of generations and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.term: μῦθον οὐ μῦθον, ἀλλὰ ὄντα λόγον
choices.english: a story not a story, but a true account
choices.why: Preserves the wordplay and the contrast between fictional tale and factual narrative; 'true account' renders λόγος as factual report.
rejected: a myth not a myth but a real story
a tale not a tale but a true word

choices.why: In early Christian usage φωτίζω means to baptize, as the context of the seal of the Lord confirms.
Baptismal seal terminology; kept literal to preserve the sacramental image.
ἄστομος means refusing the bit; 'hard-mouthed' captures the image of a horse that will not be controlled.
Keeps the baptismal metaphor of tears as a second baptism, which is central to Clement's point about repentance.
Kept literal; Clement personifies repentance as an angel or messenger that one receives in this life.

pass_b_english: And so that you may take courage, having truly repented in this way, that a worthy hope of salvation remains for you, listen to a story that is not a story, but a true account handed down about John the apostle and preserved in memory. For after the tyrant died, John returned from the island of Patmos to Ephesus. He used to go out, when invited, to the neighboring regions of the Gentiles, in some places to appoint bishops, in others to fit together whole churches, in others to choose by lot one of those indicated by the Spirit. So he came also to one of the cities not far away, whose name some even mention, and after refreshing the brothers in other matters, he looked at the appointed bishop and saw a young man able in body, pleasing in appearance, and fervent in soul. "This one," he said, "I entrust to you with all earnestness, before the church and Christ as witness." The bishop accepted him and promised everything, and again John insisted on the same things and bore witness. Then John departed for Ephesus, and the bishop took the young man entrusted to him home, nourished him, kept him close, cherished him, and finally baptized him. After this he relaxed his greater care and watchfulness, since he had set upon him the perfect safeguard, the seal of the Lord. But the young man seized freedom before the right time, and certain idle and dissolute companions of his own age, familiar with evils, corrupted him. First they drew him in through lavish banquets. Then they took him along when they went out at night for robbery, and then they demanded that he join them in something greater. He gradually grew accustomed to it, and because of the greatness of his nature he bolted like an unbridled and strong horse leaving the straight road and biting the bit, and was carried all the more violently toward the pits. Despairing completely of salvation in God, he no longer planned anything small, but since he had already perished once, he resolved to suffer the same fate as the others. Taking these very companions and forming a band of robbers, he was a ready robber chief, the most violent, the most murderous, the most savage. Time passed, and when some need arose they called John back. When he had settled the other matters for which he had come, he said, "Come now, bishop, give back to us the deposit which I and Christ entrusted to you before the church over which you preside, as witness." The bishop was at first astonished, thinking he was being falsely accused about money which he had not received, and he could neither believe about what he did not have nor disbelieve John. But when John said, "I demand the young man and the soul of the brother," the bishop groaned from deep within and wept a little, and said, "He is dead." "How, and by what death?" "He is dead to God," he said. "For he went away wicked and ruined and, in sum, a robber, and now instead of the church he has seized the mountain with a band like an army." The apostle tore his clothing and struck his head with a great lamentation. "A fine guard," he said, "I left for the soul of the brother! But let a horse be ready for me now, and let someone be my guide on the road." He rode out, just as he was, straight from the church. When he came to the place, he was seized by the robbers' lookout, neither fleeing nor resisting, but crying out, "This is why I have come: lead me to your chief." The chief was waiting, armed as he was. But when he recognized John approaching, he turned in shame to flee. John pursued him at full speed, forgetting his own age, crying out, "Why do you flee from me, child, from your own father, the naked, the old man? Have mercy on me, child; do not be afraid. You still have hopes of life. I will give an account to Christ for you. If it is necessary, I will willingly endure your death, as the Lord did for us. For you I will give my own life in exchange. Stop, believe: Christ sent me." When the young man heard this, he first stood looking down. Then he threw away his weapons. Then, trembling, he wept bitterly. When the old man approached, he embraced him, defending himself with groans as best he could and being baptized a second time with his tears, hiding his face in shame and showing only his right hand. But John, pledging and swearing that he had found forgiveness for him from the Savior, praying, falling on his knees, kissing that very right hand as cleansed by repentance, led him back to the church. And with abundant prayers he interceded for him, with constant fastings he struggled alongside him, and with varied consolations of words he soothed his mind, and he did not leave, as they say, until he had restored him to the church, giving a great example of true repentance and a great sign of regeneration, a visible proof of resurrection.

The angels rejoice with radiant ones, singing hymns, opening the heavens. And before all things the Savior himself comes to meet them, welcoming them, offering light without shadow, without ceasing, leading them into the bosom of the Father, into eternal life, into the kingdom of heaven. Let a person believe these things, both the disciples of God and God as guarantor, the prophecies, the gospels, the apostolic words. Living with these and giving ear to them and practicing their works, at the very moment of departure he will see the end and the demonstration of the teachings. For the one who receives the angel of repentance here will not repent then, when he leaves the body, nor will he be put to shame when he sees the Savior coming with his own glory and his army. He does not fear the fire. But if someone chooses to continue sinning continually in pleasures and prefers the luxury here to eternal life, and turns away when the Savior offers forgiveness, let him no longer blame God or wealth or his fall, but his own soul, which perishes willingly. But to the one who looks toward salvation and longs for it and asks with shamelessness and force, the good Father in the heavens will grant the true purification and the unchangeable life. To him, through the child Jesus Christ, the Lord of the living and the dead, and through the Holy Spirit, be glory, honor, power, eternal majesty, both now and to generations of generations and to the ages of ages. Amen.
notes: The source text contains a lacuna marked by asterisks before φαιδροῖς γεγηθότες; the preceding context is missing, so the clause begins abruptly with 'rejoicing with bright ones'.

problems.why: Greek says he showed only his right hand; English reverses the sense.
problems.ruling: μόνην ἀποκρύπτων τὴν δεξιάν means concealing only his right hand, not hiding it; English reverses the sense.

problems.source_quote: ὁ δὲ πρεσβύτερος ἀναλαβὼν οἴκαδε τὸν παραδοθέντα νεανίσκον ἔτρεφε, συνεῖχεν. ἔθαλπε, τὸ τελευταῖον ἐφώτισε…
problems.why: The source does not mention baptism at this point; baptism occurs later after John’s intervention.
problems.fix: remove "and finally baptized him" from this sentence
problems.ruling: ἐφώτισε means enlightened/illuminated, not baptized; baptism is later (βαπτιζόμενος ἐκ δευτέρου).

edits.old: cherished him, and finally baptized him.
edits.new: cherished him, and finally enlightened him.

fixed: Changed 'hiding only his right hand' to 'showing only his right hand' because the Greek 'μόνην ἀποκρύπτων τὴν δεξιάν' means he concealed everything except his right hand, i.e., he showed only his right hand.

Changed 'and finally baptized him' to 'and finally enlightened him' because the Greek 'ἐφώτισε' means 'enlightened' (a common patristic term for baptism, but the literal word is 'enlightened'), and the source does not explicitly say 'baptized' here; the later 'being baptized a second time with tears' confirms baptism had occurred, but the verb here is 'enlightened'.

problems.quote: like a hard-mouthed and strong horse
problems.fix: like a mouth‑less and strong horse

problems.why: Confirmed error: ἀποκρύπτων means 'hiding', not 'showing'. English reverses the meaning.

problems.quote: and again John insisted on the same things and bore witness
problems.source_quote: τοῦ δὲ δεχομένου ... καὶ πάλιν τὰ αὐτὰ διετείνατο καὶ διεμαρτύρατο
problems.why: The subject is the bishop (the elder), not John; John is not the one insisting
problems.fix: and the bishop continued in the same way and bore witness
problems.ruling: διετείνατο καὶ διεμαρτύρατο: subject is δεχομένου (the bishop), not John; translation wrongly attributes the insisting to John.

problems.why: The Greek says the elder cherished and praised the young man; there is no mention of ‘enlightening’
problems.ruling: ἐφώτισε means 'enlightened/instructed'; 'praised' is wrong, and 'finally' for τὸ τελευταῖον is defensible but 'enlightened' is the correct sense.

edits.old: like a hard-mouthed and strong horse
edits.new: like a mouth-less and strong horse

edits.old: and again John insisted on the same things and bore witness
edits.new: and again the bishop insisted on the same things and bore witness

fixed: ἄστομος means 'mouth-less', not 'hard-mouthed'; corrected to 'mouth-less and strong horse'.

problems.why: Greek says he uncovered/opened the right hand, not hid it; opposite meaning.

edits.new: with varied consolations of words he soothed his mind

fixed: The source uses πρεσβύτερος for the same person earlier called ἐπίσκοπος; the brief notes the bishop is 'called both elder and bishop in the story.' Using 'bishop' consistently is clearer.
The source has ἄστομος, literally 'mouthless,' but the sense is 'unbridled' or 'hard-mouthed' (a horse that ignores the bit). 'Unbridled' fits the context of a horse bolting from the road.
The source has φαιδροῖς γεγηθότες, 'rejoicing with bright ones,' a fragment after a lacuna. Adding 'The angels' as subject clarifies the sentence.
The source has μόνην ἀποκρύπτων τὴν δεξιάν, 'hiding only his right hand.' The young man hides his face in shame, leaving only his right hand visible for John to kiss. The edit clarifies the gesture.
The source has σειρῆσι λόγων, 'cords of words.' 'Charms' suggests magic; 'consolations' better fits the pastoral context of John soothing the young man's mind.
The source has γνώρισμα and τρόπαιον. 'Mark' and 'trophy' are literal but odd; 'sign' and 'visible proof' better convey the sense of a public demonstration of regeneration and resurrection.

last_rejected.quote: relaxed his greater care and watchfulness, since he had set upon him the perfect safeguard, the seal of the Lord.
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ μετὰ τοῦτο ὑφῆκε τῆς πλείονος ἐπιμελείας καὶ παραφυλακῆς, ὡς τὸ τέλειον αὐτῷ φυλακτήριον ἐπιστήσας, τὴν σφραγῖδα τοῦ κυρίου.
last_rejected.why: Greek says he gave greater care and guard, not relaxed it.
last_rejected.fix: and after this he gave him greater care and watchfulness, since he had set upon him the perfect safeguard, the seal of the Lord.
last_rejected.ruling: ὑφῆκε means 'let go/relaxed'; ὡς = 'as/considering', not 'since'. Meaning preserved adequately.

last_rejected.quote: the young man seized freedom before the right time, and certain idle and dissolute companions of his own age, familiar with evils, corrupted him.
last_rejected.source_quote: τῷ δὲ ἀνέσεως πρὸ ὥρας λαβομένῳ προσφθείρονταί τινες ἥλικες ἀργοὶ καὶ ἀπερρωγότες, ἐθάδες κακῶν·
last_rejected.why: Greek indicates youths attached to the young man before the appointed time; the English makes the young man the agent of “seizing freedom”.
last_rejected.fix: before the appointed time, certain idle and dissolute youths attached themselves to the young man, corrupting him.
last_rejected.ruling: τῷ...λαβομένῳ is dative 'to him who had taken freedom'; English conveys this adequately as narrative.
